Dear Mr. Kapadia,

I hope you are keeping well. I am writing on behalf of Hyderabad Cloudserve Pvt. Ltd., with whom, I understand, your team has had a pleasant working relationship over the past two years. My client holds you in high regard, which is precisely why this message is being sent in a spirit of resolution rather than confrontation.

As per the records shared with us, the hosting charges for the quarters ending March and June 2026 (Rs. 9,24,500/- including GST) remain outstanding. My client has attempted to reach your accounts team on four occasions between 15 July and 28 September without receiving a firm commitment.

Ananya Rao

subject: Deficiency in service - final communication before filing complaint
body:
To the Customer Grievance Officer, Nexora,

I am writing for the fifth and final time regarding my order NX-704412, placed on 2 August 2026 for a clinic management system licence for my hospital in Coimbatore at a cost of Rs. 1,12,000. The software was to go live on 20 August. It is now 22 October, the module for patient billing still does not work, and I have lost at least three weeks of patient records because of a faulty data migration that your engineers carried out without taking a backup.

This constitutes deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. I have kept all email exchanges, call logs and a record of the data loss, and I am prepared to place them before the District Commission. I am seeking a full refund, compensation of Rs. 2,00,000 for the loss and harassment, and written confirmation of the recovery of my data.

If I do not receive a substantive reply within 10 days of this email, I will file a complaint without further notice.

Dr. Prakash Venkataraman
Venkataraman Multispeciality Clinic, RS Puram, Coimbatore
